401.description: Unauthorized: `UNAUTHENTICATED`. This route needs no access token, but one that is sent is checked, and an expired or unaccepted one is refused. Send no `Authorization` header here.

Unauthorized: `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for every refused sign-in (a wrong password, an unknown address, a locked account: one answer for all, on purpose); `UNAUTHENTICATED` when an `Authorization` header is sent whose token is not accepted. No `WWW-Authenticate`.

503.description: Service Unavailable: `HASHING_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, with `Retry-After: 1`. Password hashing is momentarily full; retry the same request.

401.description: Unauthorized: `UNAUTHENTICATED`. This route needs no access token, but one that is sent is checked, and an expired or unaccepted one is refused. Send no `Authorization` header here.

Unauthorized: `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` for a refresh token that is unknown, expired or revoked: sign in again. `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` for one already exchanged: every session of its family has been ended, so drop the stored credentials and sign in again. `UNAUTHENTICATED` when an `Authorization` header is sent whose token is not accepted.

410.description: Gone: `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. The link was real but is past its hour or was already used. Ask for a new one. Only a `token` is answered 410; an `email` and `code` never are.

422.description: Unprocessable: `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a body that is not exactly one of a `token`, or an `email` and a six-digit `code`, or for the new `password` (`VALID_PASSWORD`, `NOT_BREACHED`); that refusal spends nothing. `PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID` for a token that matches nothing, and for every refused code: no such account, a wrong code, or one expired (15 minutes), burned (5 wrong tries) or spent. One answer for all of them, on purpose; ask for a new email.

503.description: Service Unavailable: `HASHING_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, with `Retry-After: 1`. Password hashing is momentarily full; retry the same request. The link or the code is not spent. Or `CODE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, with `Retry-After: 60`, for an `email` and `code` only: the limit on typed codes cannot be read just now, so no code is checked. The code is not spent or counted, and the answer is the same whether the address has an account. The link in the same email still works; offer it, or try the code again after the wait.

410.description: Gone: `VERIFICATION_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. The link was real but is past its 24 hours or was already used. Ask for a new one. Only a `token` is answered 410; an `email` and `code` never are.

422.description: Unprocessable: `VALIDATION_FAILED` for a body that is not exactly one of a `token`, or an `email` and a six-digit `code`. `VERIFICATION_TOKEN_INVALID` for a token that matches nothing, and for every refused code: no such account, a wrong code, or one expired (15 minutes), burned (5 wrong tries) or spent. One answer for all of them, on purpose; ask for a new email.

post.description: Ends the bond for both members, with the same `204` as `POST /bonds/{bondId}/leave`, and keeps the two accounts from being paired again. Also accepted on a bond that has already ended, and may be repeated. **The body is required, and so is `withdrawEntries`.** When it is `true`, every entry the caller wrote in this bond is withdrawn: the entries are ERASED, for both members, and this cannot be undone. Send `{"withdrawEntries": false}` to keep them. When the flag is absent or null, or there is no body, the answer is `400 MALFORMED_REQUEST` and nothing is ended or withdrawn; a caller who is not a member is answered `404` first. A later call with `true` withdraws what an earlier one kept. A body with any other key, with the key twice, or with a value that is not JSON true or false is `400 MALFORMED_REQUEST`; nothing is ignored. A `Content-Type` that is not JSON is `415`, with or without a body.

get.description:
The days of the bond on which the caller has something to see, newest first. A day is listed when it holds an entry the caller wrote, or one that has been revealed to them; an erased entry still counts, and is returned as its tombstone.

**Only a null `nextCursor` means the end.** A page's `items` can be shorter than `limit` while `nextCursor` is not null, because a page is also bounded by its size. A page with a `nextCursor` holds at least one day, with one exception: a single request reads at most about a thousand days, and with `favourites=true` a request that reaches that bound answers with what it has found, which can be nothing. Keep asking with the cursor until it is null.

**A day's `status` does not say whether there is anything to draw.** A day whose author deleted their only entry is still listed, for that author alone, with their tombstone as `myEntry`; once that day has closed it carries `status: EMPTY`. Draw a day from its entries, not from its status.

parameters.description: The most days to return. A page can hold fewer and still not be the last: it is also bounded by its size. Only a null `nextCursor` means the end.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of an earlier page, unchanged: the days before that page's last. Opaque; do not build or alter one. It carries no bond and no caller, only a position, so it grants nothing.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Start at this calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or the nearest earlier day: for jumping to a month. With `cursor` as well, both apply.
parameters.name: until

parameters.description: `true` for only the days holding an entry the caller has bookmarked and can still read. Only the caller's own bookmarks are ever considered.
parameters.name: favourites

parameters.description: The `ETag` of a response to this same request that the client still holds (RFC 9110 §13.1.2). If it is still current the answer is `304` with no body. A value that is not current, or is not a tag, is ignored and the whole response is sent.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

ETag.description: Strong validator (RFC 9110 §8.8.3) of this response body exactly as it was sent to this caller. Opaque: keep the entire value and send it back as `If-None-Match`. It changes whenever anything in the body would, and is not the other member's. Sent with `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`.

304.description: Not Modified: what the client holds under the `If-None-Match` it sent is still exactly what would be sent. No body.

406.description: Not Acceptable: the request's `Accept` header admits no JSON. Decided from that header alone, before the caller's membership is looked at, so it is the same response for a member, for somebody who is not one and for a bond that does not exist. It carries no `ETag`.

get.description: One day exactly as `GET /bonds/{bondId}/days` lists it: the same object, for the same caller. `404 DAY_NOT_FOUND` for every date that is not in the caller's archive, whatever the reason. Today is not in it until the caller has written or the day has revealed, so read today from `GET /bonds/{bondId}/today`. As in the feed, a day's `status` does not say whether there is anything to draw: draw a day from its entries.

parameters.description: A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A date that is not in the caller's archive is `404 DAY_NOT_FOUND`, whatever the reason, and so is a value that is not a date.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: The `ETag` of a response to this same request that the client still holds (RFC 9110 §13.1.2). If it is still current the answer is `304` with no body. A value that is not current, or is not a tag, is ignored and the whole response is sent.

parameters.description: A client-chosen key, unique per retried request (doc 06 §1). A replay of the same key with the same request returns the first attempt's status and the same resource, re-read and rendered from its current state — never a stored copy. A replay is authorised as a read of the result: a caller who may still read it gets it back even if a new write would now be refused, a caller who may no longer read it gets the read's refusal, and a resource erased since is returned as its tombstone. Only a success is recorded; a request that was refused may be corrected and retried under the same key. The same key with a different method, path or body is 422; the same key while the first attempt is still in flight is 409. The key itself is 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters (a UUID is the usual choice); a malformed one is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with an `errors` entry naming this header, and so is a missing one wherever this parameter is marked required. Where it is optional, leaving it out makes an ordinary, unrecorded request.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when this response answers a replay of an earlier request under the same Idempotency-Key (doc 06 §1): nothing was written again, and the body is the resource as it stands now. Absent on a fresh response.

post.description: Ends the bond for both members. It stays readable to both, and takes no further entries. The body is optional. **When `withdrawEntries` is absent or null, or there is no body, the caller's entries are kept.** When it is `true`, every entry the caller wrote in this bond is erased, for both members, and this cannot be undone. The other route that ends a bond has no default: there the flag is required. `409 BOND_ARCHIVED` on a bond that has already ended, and nothing is withdrawn then. A body with any other key, with the key twice, or with a value that is not JSON true, false or null is `400 MALFORMED_REQUEST`; nothing is ignored. A `Content-Type` that is not JSON is `415`, with or without a body.

get.description:
The bond's milestones at 7, 30, 100 and 365 complete days: days on which both members wrote, counted over the bond's whole life. A day a freeze covered is not a complete day, and a broken streak loses no milestone. `achieved` lists each one reached, oldest first, with the date of the day that reached it. Today counts once it has revealed, by the same rule as the streak's numbers.

`next` is the next threshold and nothing else. It is null once all four are reached, and whenever the bond takes no writes from the caller: it has ended, the caller has left, or it is counting down to deletion. `achieved` is kept when the bond ends.

The days of the bond dated today's month and day in an earlier year, newest first, each in the feed's day shape. Today is the bond's date. 29 February is found on 29 February only. A day is included when an entry on it can be read in full by the caller; a day of tombstones is not.

Empty when the bond takes no writes from the caller: it has ended, the caller has left, or it is counting down to deletion. There is no cursor: it is every such day, within the size of one response.

"Remember when": the days of the bond most relevant to a question, most relevant first, each day whole and in the feed's day shape. Two rankings of the entries the caller can read in full are fused: by the question's words, and by its meaning, when the bond's semantic search is on and the meaning can be read in time. When it cannot (the setting is off, no provider is configured, the provider fails or is slow), the answer is the words' ranking alone, still `200`: the client renders one state. Only entries a person wrote are returned, never generated text, and nothing says which entry of a day was relevant or why.

There is no cursor: it is one answer, not a feed. It may hold fewer days than `limit`, or none, because a day is shown only when the caller can read the relevant entry in full, and the answer is bounded by its size. The caller's own entry is found before it is revealed; the partner's only once it has been.

`q` is never echoed in a refusal, and the response is never to be stored. Thirty questions an hour per account: each may be sent to the embedding provider.

parameters.description: The question, in plain words, read as the search box reads `q`: 1 to 100 characters (graphemes, counted on the NFKC-normalised, trimmed text), at most 1024 UTF-8 octets, not only space, no U+0000. `maxLength` states the octet cap in UTF-16 characters, a coarse hint. A value that cannot be searched is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on `q`, and is never sent back. A value whose percent-decoded bytes are not UTF-8 is 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST, for a member and a stranger alike, after authentication and before the membership check.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: The most days to return, 1 to 20. Anything else is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on `limit`.
parameters.name: limit

get.description:
The days of the bond on which one entry the caller can read in full holds every word of `q`, newest first, each day whole and in the feed's day shape. Whole words, compared without case or accents (`cafe` finds `Café`); no prefixes, no stemming, no operators. The caller's own entry is found before it is revealed; the partner's only once it has been.

**Only a null `nextCursor` means the end.** A page can hold fewer days than `limit` and still have a `nextCursor`, because it is also bounded by its size. There is no count of matches, and nothing says which entry of a day matched or where: a client that highlights does so itself.

`q` is never echoed in a refusal, and the response is never to be stored.

parameters.description: The words to look for: 1 to 100 characters (graphemes, counted on the NFKC-normalised, trimmed text), at most 1024 UTF-8 octets, not only space, no U+0000. `maxLength` states the octet cap in UTF-16 characters, a coarse hint. A value that cannot be searched is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on `q`, and is never sent back. A value whose percent-decoded bytes are not UTF-8 is 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST, for a member and a stranger alike, after authentication and before the membership check. Words with no letter or digit in them (punctuation, emoji) match nothing.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: The most days to return, as on the feed. Only a null `nextCursor` means the end.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of an earlier page of this search, unchanged. The feed's own cursor: a position, nothing else.
parameters.name: cursor

delete.description: Calls off a pending request to turn semantic search back on: the member who made it withdraws it, or the other declines it. `204`; nothing pending is 404.

post.description: Asks to turn the bond's semantic search back on, or agrees to the other member's request. `202` with the bond: on a paired bond nothing changes until the other member makes the same request, which turns it on at once; on a bond still waiting for its second member it is on at once. Asking again, or asking while it is on, changes nothing. Once on, the bond's entries are embedded in the background, and until then they are found by their words alone. A bond that has ended is 409 BOND_ARCHIVED.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when this response answers a replay of an earlier request under the same Idempotency-Key (doc 06 §1): nothing was written again, and the body is the resource as it stands now. Absent on a fresh response.

delete.description: Removes the caller's bookmark. Repeatable: no bookmark is success, and so is an entry that has since been erased. `404` is every entry the caller was never shown, the same as for an id that does not exist. `409 FAVOURITE_BUSY` means another operation holds the bookmark; retry the removal. It is never given for an entry the caller is shown as erased: there the answer is `204`. Allowed on a bond that has ended.

put.description: Marks the entry as the caller's own bookmark. The other member is never shown it, in any response. Repeatable: a second mark changes nothing and is `204`. Only an entry the caller is shown with `status: REVEALED` can be marked. `409 ENTRY_NOT_REVEALED` is the caller's own entry that has not been revealed. `409 ENTRY_IMMUTABLE` is an entry that has been erased, or is being erased: a tombstone. `404` is every entry the caller was never shown, the same as for an id that does not exist. A body, if one is sent, is ignored. Allowed on a bond that has ended.

delete.description: Takes the caller's reaction back. Repeatable: no reaction is success, and so is an entry that has since been erased, or one the caller wrote. `404` is every entry the caller was never shown, the same as for an id that does not exist. `409 BOND_ARCHIVED` is the partner's entry on a bond that has ended, or that the caller has left: the reaction stays, and is still shown. `409 REACTION_BUSY` means another operation holds the reaction, which can be the caller's own request still running (two removals at once, or one over the caller's own `PUT`); retry the removal. Neither is given for an entry the caller is shown as erased, or for one the caller wrote: there the answer is `204`, on a bond that has ended too.

put.description: Leaves the caller's reaction on their partner's entry: one per member per entry, so a second one replaces the first. The other member is shown it, as the entry's `reaction`, and is not shown when it was left. Repeatable. Only the partner's entry that the caller is shown with `status: REVEALED` takes one. `409 REACTION_ON_OWN_ENTRY` is an entry the caller wrote. `409 ENTRY_IMMUTABLE` is an entry that has been erased, or is being erased: a tombstone. `409 BOND_ARCHIVED` is a bond that has ended. `404` is every entry the caller was never shown, the same as for an id that does not exist. A `type` that is absent, null or not one of the listed names, exactly, is `422`. A body with any other key, or with `type` twice, is `400`; nothing is ignored. A body with no `Content-Type`, or one that is not JSON, is `415`. A body is judged before the entry is looked at.

post.description: Reports the caller's partner's entry to a person, who reviews it, with its photo and voice note. `201` with the report's id. From that moment the entry's photo and voice note are held back from the caller pending review: the caller is shown them as PROCESSING, as anything held back is; the author is shown them as NOT_SHARED, as anything held back is, and is never told that a report was made, or by whom. The entry's words are not hidden. Only the partner's entry the caller is shown, in full or as a tombstone, can be reported, on a bond that has ended too. `409 REPORT_ON_OWN_ENTRY` is an entry the caller wrote. `404` is every entry the caller was never shown, the same as for an id that does not exist. An `Idempotency-Key` is required: repeating the request with the same key is the same report, `201` again with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and nothing filed twice. A `reason` that is absent, null or not one of the listed names, exactly, is `422`, and so is a `detail` that is blank or longer than 500 characters. A body is judged before the entry is looked at. Ten reports a day per account.

delete.description: Calls off the pending account deletion. `204`. `404 NOT_FOUND` when there is nothing to cancel, whether nothing was requested, it was already cancelled, or `cancellableUntil` has passed: one answer for all, because there is nothing the person can do about any of them.

post.description: Asks for the signed-in account to be deleted (FR-008). Nothing is destroyed now: `202` answers with `requestedAt`, `cancellableUntil` (14 days later) and `deleteBy` (30 days later, FR-008's bound). Until `cancellableUntil` the person can still sign in and use the app, and `DELETE` calls it off; other sessions are not ended. From `cancellableUntil` it cannot be cancelled, and within the hour the account is deleted: the address and name are erased and the account can no longer sign in; every entry its owner wrote becomes a blank placeholder in each shared archive, so the other person's days and streak stay as they were; their bookmarks, reactions, photos and voice notes, devices and sessions are deleted, their open support messages emptied, and every bond they are still in ends as if they had left it. Asking again while one is pending is the same `202` with the same dates. The current `password` is required: wrong is `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (the session is fine; do not sign out), absent or blank is `422`. A confirmed address is emailed once per request, saying when and how to cancel. Five an hour per account, wrong passwords included: the sixth is `429` with `Retry-After`.

get.description: The caller's most recently requested export, as `GET /me/export/{exportId}` answers it, so that a client can show its state after a restart without keeping the id. `404 NOT_FOUND` if the caller has never asked for one.

post.description: Asks for a copy of everything the signed-in person is entitled to (FR-009). Nothing is built when this returns: `202` answers `PREPARING` with the export's `id`, a job builds it, usually within minutes, and a confirmed address is emailed when it is `READY` (the email carries no link: the person downloads it in the app). Asking again while one is `PREPARING` is the same export, `202` with the same `id`; asking after it is `READY`, `EXPIRED` or `FAILED` starts a new one. Allowed whatever state the person's bonds are in, ended or left included (BR-9). The archive is a zip of `moyi-export.json` (the account and its consents; every bond the person is or was in, with every day of its archive exactly as the app shows it to them, their partner's entries only once revealed to them, and every entry withdrawn on a block or a leave, theirs or their partner's, as a blank placeholder; their bookmarks and the reactions on each entry; their support messages; and any recorded administrator access), the photos and voice notes it names under `media/`, and a `README.txt`. Three new exports a day per account; a repeat while one is `PREPARING` spends none: the fourth new one is `429` with `Retry-After`.

get.description: One of the caller's exports, as it is now. `downloadUrl`, `expiresAt` and `sizeBytes` are present only while it is `READY`. An export past its 24 hours is `EXPIRED` from that moment, and so is a `READY` one when entries are withdrawn in one of the person's bonds (a block or a leave that withdraws): its archive held words that are gone for both people, so it is deleted, and the person asks again. An `exportId` that is someone else's and one that does not exist are the same `404 NOT_FOUND`.

post.description: The caller accepts the current Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, the versions `GET /meta/legal` names. No body, and none is read: the versions recorded are the server's. `204` whether or not anything was new; a version accepted before keeps the moment it was first accepted. Afterwards `GET /me`'s `legalAccepted` names the current versions.

get.description: The current Terms of Service, Privacy Policy and data-processing summary: each a `version` and the absolute `url` it is read at. Public: no token is needed, because sign-up shows them before there is an account. A `version` is an opaque label (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`; at most 40): compare it with `GET /me`'s `legalAccepted`, never parse it. Where the two differ, ask the person to accept again and send `POST /me/legal-consent`. The data-processing summary is shown, never accepted on its own. Registration records the Terms and Privacy versions this answer names, whatever the request says.

parameters.description: The `ETag` of an earlier answer the client still holds. If it is still current the answer is `304` with no body; any other value is ignored and the whole response is sent.
parameters.name: If-None-Match

ETag.description: Strong validator of this response body (RFC 9110 §8.8.3). Opaque: keep the whole value and send it back as `If-None-Match`. The same for every caller; sent with `Cache-Control: public, no-cache`.

304.description: Not Modified: the documents are still those the client holds under that tag. No body.

ETag.description: Strong validator of this response body (RFC 9110 §8.8.3). Opaque: keep the whole value and send it back as `If-None-Match`. The same for every caller; sent with `Cache-Control: public, no-cache`.

401.description: Unauthorized: `UNAUTHENTICATED`. This route needs no access token, but one that is sent is checked, and an expired or unaccepted one is refused. Send no `Authorization` header here.

post.description: Writes to Moyi's support, as the signed-in account: the message becomes a ticket a person reads, and `201` answers with its id and when it arrived. Once it is stored, an acknowledgement email is attempted once, to the account's address if that address has been confirmed; it gives the id as a reference and never repeats the subject or the body. It is best effort and not promised: it is not retried if the email provider fails. A signed-out person cannot use this route. An `Idempotency-Key` is optional: repeating the request with the same key is the same ticket, `201` again with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, filed once and acknowledged at most once; without a key, each request is a new ticket. A replay spends one of the five a day as well, so a retry can be `429`: wait for `Retry-After`, then the same key returns the same ticket. A `subject` or `body` that is absent, null, blank or too long is `422` naming the field; so is a `reference` that is empty, too long or not visible ASCII. Five messages a day per account, refused ones and replays included: the sixth is `429` with `Retry-After`.

parameters.description: A client-chosen key, unique per retried request (doc 06 §1). A replay of the same key with the same request returns the first attempt's status and the same resource, re-read and rendered from its current state — never a stored copy. A replay is authorised as a read of the result: a caller who may still read it gets it back even if a new write would now be refused, a caller who may no longer read it gets the read's refusal, and a resource erased since is returned as its tombstone. Only a success is recorded; a request that was refused may be corrected and retried under the same key. The same key with a different method, path or body is 422; the same key while the first attempt is still in flight is 409. The key itself is 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters (a UUID is the usual choice); a malformed one is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with an `errors` entry naming this header, and so is a missing one wherever this parameter is marked required. Where it is optional, leaving it out makes an ordinary, unrecorded request.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true` when this response answers a replay of an earlier request under the same Idempotency-Key (doc 06 §1): nothing was written again, and the body is the resource as it stands now. Absent on a fresh response.

settlesAt.description: The earliest this day can be decided: its end on the bond's calendar plus the late-entry grace (twelve hours by default; issue #132). An entry written on this day and sent before then counts for it; one sent after counts for the day it is sent. The day is decided on the next run of the close job after this, usually within minutes; until then a lone entry is not yet unlocked to the partner, and a missed day not yet counted. Never null.

pendingSemanticSearchRequest.description: A request by one member to turn semantic search back on, waiting for the other to agree through the same `POST`. It lapses at `expiresAt`, seven days after it was made.

semanticSearchEnabled.description: Whether the bond's entries are embedded so that search and "Remember when" also find by meaning. On by default. While on, the words of each entry are sent to the embedding provider, once a provider is configured. Either member turns it off alone; on again needs both.

downloadUrl.description: Only while `READY`: a signed URL that downloads the zip without a bearer, good until `expiresAt` (FR-094). Treat it as the archive itself: anyone holding it can download it.

expiresAt.description: Only while `READY`: when the download URL stops working and the archive is deleted (`readyAt` + 24 h).

readyAt.description: When it became `READY`; null while `PREPARING`, and for a `FAILED` one.

sizeBytes.description: Only while `READY`: the zip's size in bytes.

status.description: `PREPARING` until it is built (usually within minutes), then `READY` for 24 hours, then `EXPIRED`; `FAILED` if it could not be built after three tries (ask again).

image.description: The entry's photo, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

reaction.description: The reaction on this entry: the one left by the member who did not write it, or null. Both members are sent the same value. Always null on an erased entry.

voice.description: The entry's voice note, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

DeletedPartnerEntryResponse.description: The other member's entry, with every field an entry has, when its `status` is `DELETED`.

password.description: The account's current password, typed again. Absent, null or blank is `422`; wrong is `401`.

withdrawEntries.description: Whether to withdraw the caller's own entries in this bond: every one is erased, for both members, and this cannot be undone. What an absent or null value means depends on the route; each operation's description says. Only JSON true, false or null is accepted.

EntryImageResponse.description: An entry's photo as the caller is shown it. url, width and height are present when status is READY: to its author once it is ready, to the other member only once it has also passed moderation; until then it is PROCESSING to them, whatever the reason. NOT_SHARED is its author's alone: the photo is held back, for review, from the other member, who is shown PROCESSING and never told it was removed; url, width and height are still given, unless it was blocked outright, when they are null. sensitive is true when the photo passed moderation with adult nudity found: show it blurred, behind a tap to view; it is false otherwise, and always false unless status is READY. The url is a signed GET, valid for at least 24 hours, ending on the hour and the same all hour, so it may be cached by; it is a credential for the photo.

EntryResponse.description: An entry with every field it has. The caller's own entry is always this shape; the other member's is `PartnerEntryResponse`.

image.description: The entry's photo, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

reaction.description: The reaction on this entry: the one left by the member who did not write it, or null. Both members are sent the same value. Always null on an erased entry.

voice.description: The entry's voice note, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

EntryVoiceResponse.description: An entry's voice note as the caller is played it. url and durationMs are present when status is READY, to its author once it is transcoded, to the other member only once it has passed moderation; until then it is PROCESSING to them, whatever the reason. NOT_SHARED is its author's alone, as a photo's: held back from the other member for review; url and durationMs are still given unless it was blocked outright. sensitive as a photo's. The url is a signed GET of an Ogg Opus file (mono, 24 kbit/s), valid for at least 24 hours, ending on the hour and the same all hour, so it may be cached by; it is a credential for the voice note. durationMs is the length of what was transcoded, at most 61.1 seconds.

waveform.description: The voice note's loudness over time, to draw: 64 levels, each 0 to 255, one per equal slice of its length in order, the RMS of that slice scaled so that the loudest is 255 (all 0 for a silent note). Measured by the server from the note it keeps, never sent by a client. Given exactly when url is; null when url is, and for a note processed before levels were measured, when the client draws its own stand-in.

FieldViolation.description: One rejected field. Never carries the rejected value.

LockedEntryResponse.description: The other member's entry while it is locked: written, and not revealed to the caller yet. It carries its author and its `status`, LOCKED, and nothing else.

PartnerEntryResponse.description: The other member's entry, as the caller is shown it. `status` says which shape this is, and the schema each value maps to is the whole of what is sent: LOCKED is an entry written and not yet revealed, and carries nothing but its author; REVEALED is the entry in full; DELETED is its tombstone, erased after it was revealed (its `text` is null). An entry erased before it was ever revealed is not shown at all: the field is null.

semanticSearchEnabled.description: Only `false` is accepted: either member turns semantic search off alone, and every vector of the bond's entries is deleted. `true` is 422 on this field (ASSERT_FALSE): turning it on needs both members, through `POST /bonds/{bondId}/semantic-search`. `false` alone is accepted on a bond that has ended, too, so that nothing more is sent to the provider; any other change to an ended bond is still 409.

text.description: FR-041: at least one character that is neither whitespace (Unicode-aware, so a lone non-breaking space does not count either) nor invisible (Unicode's Default_Ignorable_Code_Point: a text of only zero-width spaces, joiners, variation selectors and the like is refused as empty; the published `pattern` does not express this, and matches such a text), at most 8192 UTF-8 octets and at most 500 user-perceived characters (graphemes, not UTF-16 code units — an emoji sequence can be one grapheme and several of those). `maxLength` here states the octet cap in UTF-16 characters, which is not the same unit as either real limit and both are wider than this hint suggests for multi-byte text: treat it as a coarse client-side backstop, not a guarantee. The server enforces both limits exactly and is the only authority on whether a given body is accepted. The text is stored and returned exactly as sent — not normalised, not trimmed. The 500 are counted as typed, on the text as sent, untrimmed (so a typographic ellipsis counts as one, and a leading or trailing space counts too), and so are the octets. U+0000 is refused.

ProblemDetail.description: RFC 9457 problem details (doc 06 §2). Switch on `code`; `detail` is prose and may change.

allowedFrom.description: Only with `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_TOO_SOON`: the first date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, in the bond's shared time zone, `anchorTimezone`) on which the shared time zone can be changed again, from its start. Absent on every other code.

traceId.description: The id of the trace this request was served under: 32 lower-case hex digits (W3C Trace Context). The server's log lines for the request carry the same id, so quoting it to support finds them. It names a request, nothing in it, and is different on every request.

deletionRequest.description: The account deletion waiting to be carried out, with its dates, or `null` when none is. Read it on start: a client reinstalled during the 14 days draws the pending state, and its cancel, from this.

type.description: The reaction to leave, by its exact name.

displayName.description: The name the other member sees. At most 80 UTF-16 characters as sent. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed off, and what is left may not be blank, counting every Unicode space as blank (U+00A0, U+2007 and U+202F included), and may not contain a control character (Unicode category Cc: tab and newline included, a name is one line), a format character (Cf: the bidirectional controls such as U+202E, the zero-width space, word joiner, byte-order mark, soft hyphen and tag characters) except U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER and U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER, which some scripts and emoji sequences need, or an unpaired surrogate. Private-use and unassigned code points are accepted. A refused name is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` with the field's code `VALID_DISPLAY_NAME` (an empty or all-space one carries `NOT_BLANK` too). Stored as sent, trimmed and not normalised.

over18.description: The person confirms they are 18 or older (FR-011). Required, and only `true` is accepted: `false` is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`, and a body without the field is `400 MALFORMED_REQUEST`.

detail.description: Optional: anything the reviewer should know, in the reporter's words, at most 500 characters (Unicode code points). Not blank, and never shown to the other member. Kept until the report is decided, then deleted.

reason.description: Why the entry is reported, by its exact name. MINOR_SEXUAL_CONTENT is reviewed first.

withdrawEntries.description: Whether to withdraw the caller's own entries in this bond. `true` erases every one, for both members, and this cannot be undone; `false` keeps them. Required, and never null.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: Exactly one of: `token`, the value after `?token=` in the emailed link; or `email` and `code`, the address the email was sent to and the six digits in it. Anything else is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`.

code.description: The six ASCII digits from the email (surrounding space is trimmed). Good for 15 minutes, until 5 wrong tries, and until a newer email is sent; spent with the link beside it. Another shape is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` with the field's code `VALID_VERIFICATION_CODE`, and counts as no try.

email.description: The address the email was sent to, as typed (case and surrounding space do not matter). Send with `code`.

token.description: The token from the emailed link. Send it alone, without `email` or `code`.

image.description: The entry's photo, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

reaction.description: The reaction on this entry: the one left by the member who did not write it, or null. Both members are sent the same value. Always null on an erased entry.

voice.description: The entry's voice note, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

RevealedPartnerEntryResponse.description: The other member's entry, with every field an entry has, when its `status` is `REVEALED`.

reason.description: Why a FROZEN square is a rest day, and null on every other square. REST_DAY: a day the two did not both write on, covered by a banked freeze ("we used a rest day"). TIMEZONE_SHIFT: a date an approved time-zone change stepped over, which nobody could write on; no freeze was spent.

settlesAt.description: The earliest an OPEN square's day can be decided, and null on every other square (issue #132): its end on the bond's calendar plus the late-entry grace (twelve hours by default). An entry written on that day and sent before this instant still counts for it. The day is decided (complete, a rest day or missed) on the next run of the close job after this, usually within minutes, and the square stays OPEN until then, so this can be in the past. An OPEN square is today, or an earlier day not yet decided.

lastRunBrokenOn.description: The date of the missed day that ended the run lastRunLength counts, in the bond's calendar; that day is not part of the run. Null exactly when lastRunLength is.

lastRunLength.description: The length of the run the latest break ended, or null while no run has ended: "your streak ended at 21 days". A run ends on a missed day no rest day covered; a covered day, a day missed with no run, a suspended day and a day missed after the bond ended end nothing. It stays the last ended run while the next one grows, so the ended copy is for when current is 0 and this is not null. Never today: today can only extend a run. It is not longest, which is the longest run ever. At least 1.

promptId.description: The id of the prompt this entry answers, from today's `prompt` or any earlier one; optional. A value that names no prompt is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on this field. Never sent back, on any entry.

text.description: FR-041: at least one character that is neither whitespace (Unicode-aware, so a lone non-breaking space does not count either) nor invisible (Unicode's Default_Ignorable_Code_Point: a text of only zero-width spaces, joiners, variation selectors and the like is refused as empty; the published `pattern` does not express this, and matches such a text), at most 8192 UTF-8 octets and at most 500 user-perceived characters (graphemes, not UTF-16 code units — an emoji sequence can be one grapheme and several of those). `maxLength` here states the octet cap in UTF-16 characters, which is not the same unit as either real limit and both are wider than this hint suggests for multi-byte text: treat it as a coarse client-side backstop, not a guarantee. The server enforces both limits exactly and is the only authority on whether a given body is accepted. The text is stored and returned exactly as sent — not normalised, not trimmed. The 500 are counted as typed, on the text as sent, untrimmed (so a typographic ellipsis counts as one, and a leading or trailing space counts too), and so are the octets. U+0000 is refused.

image.description: The entry's photo, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

reaction.description: The reaction on this entry: the one left by the member who did not write it, or null. Both members are sent the same value. Always null on an erased entry.

voice.description: The entry's voice note, or null when it has none. Always null on an erased entry; a locked entry has no such field.

SubmittedPartnerEntryResponse.description: The other member's entry, with every field an entry has, when its `status` is `SUBMITTED`.

body.description: At most 5000 characters (Unicode code points), not blank, U+0000 refused. Kept exactly as sent, read by a person, never shown back and never repeated in the acknowledgement email.

reference.description: Optional: the reference of the error that led the person here, usually that error's `traceId`, when support was opened from an error; absent or null otherwise. 1 to 64 visible ASCII characters (0x21 to 0x7E: no space, nothing past ASCII), else `422` naming `reference`. Stored with the ticket and shown to the person answering it; never repeated in the acknowledgement email, and deleted with the words when the ticket is closed.

subject.description: At most 120 characters (Unicode code points), not blank, U+0000 refused. Kept exactly as sent, read by a person, never shown back and never repeated in the acknowledgement email.

prompt.description: The bond's prompt of the day: the same prompt for both members, each in their own language. Null when the bond takes no writes from the caller (it has ended, is counting down to deletion, or the caller has left), and when the library holds nothing for this bond. Optional to answer; dismissing it is the client's alone.

VerifyEmailRequest.description: Exactly one of: `token`, the value after `?token=` in the emailed link; or `email` and `code`, the address the email was sent to and the six digits in it. Anything else is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED`.

code.description: The six ASCII digits from the email (surrounding space is trimmed). Good for 15 minutes, until 5 wrong tries, and until a newer email is sent; spent with the link beside it. Another shape is `422 VALIDATION_FAILED` with the field's code `VALID_VERIFICATION_CODE`, and counts as no try.

email.description: The address the email was sent to, as typed (case and surrounding space do not matter). Send with `code`.

token.description: The token from the emailed link. Send it alone, without `email` or `code`.
